title: Rutland VT Home Energy Rebates 2026: Oil-Heat Homes and Efficiency Vermont
desc: Rutland, Vermont home rebates for 2026: heat pump discounts, weatherization up to $3,000 ($7,000 if income-eligible), battery and EV rebates, for a city where 69% of homes burn oil.
h1: Home Energy Rebates in Rutland, Vermont
lead: Rutland is the clearest oil-heat city of the five Vermont cities we cover, and half its homes predate 1940. It also has the coldest record low. The rebates here are mostly Efficiency Vermont's and Green Mountain Power's, and the weatherization case is strong.
cards_heading: The rebates that matter most in Rutland
cards_intro: We re-read Efficiency Vermont's rebate list and Green Mountain Power's program pages on October 5, 2026. Rutland is Green Mountain Power territory. Amounts are maximums.

cards.title: Heat pump
cards.note: Efficiency Vermont instant discounts by system type, plus up to $600 for controls. Green Mountain Power adds $2,000 per condenser for households at or under 80% of area median income ($89,200 for four in Rutland County).

cards.title: Weatherization
cards.note: 75% of qualifying insulation and air sealing, higher cap if income-eligible, while funding lasts.

cards.title: Heat pump water heater
cards.note: Efficiency Vermont, through the Green Mountain Power page for your area.

cards.title: Home battery
cards.note: Green Mountain Power's Bring Your Own Device program pays by the kW of storage you share at peaks, with $100 more per kW for some solar retrofits.

cards.title: Electric vehicle and charger
cards.note: Green Mountain Power: up to $2,500 for an all-electric vehicle, and up to $650 toward a home charger installation if you buy or lease in 2026.

cards.title: Appliances
cards.note: Efficiency Vermont rebates on thermostats, dryers, dehumidifiers and stoves, and Green Mountain Power's $200 induction cooktop rebate.

after_cards: Statewide pages cover solar, batteries, EV chargers, appliances and thermostats and windows and doors.
sections: The Census Bureau's 2020 to 2024 American Community Survey counts 7,414 occupied homes in Rutland. 5,124 (69%) burn oil, 1,111 (15%) propane, 605 (8%) electricity, 184 wood and 366 (5%) piped gas. 4,287 of 8,517 housing units (50%) were built in 1939 or earlier. Oil plus old buildings is where weatherization pays back most, and where a cold-climate heat pump has the most fuel to displace.

55% of households own and 45% rent. 49% of units are detached houses, 2,500 sit in two-, three- and four-unit buildings and 1,496 in larger buildings. Efficiency Vermont's heat pump rebates are open to rental properties but its income bonus is not, and its Home Performance weatherization offer covers existing one-to-four-unit homes, a size that fits much of Rutland's rental stock.

The average January low is -10.2°C and the coldest day between 2015 and 2024 reached -34.8°C. Ask any contractor what the unit they propose delivers at the bottom of its range and what backup remains for those nights.

For an oil-heated Rutland house the usual sequence is weatherization, then a ductless heat pump with integrated controls in the main living area, then the heat pump water heater so the boiler can rest in summer. Each step has its own rebate, and the earlier ones make the later ones smaller and cheaper.

Three deadlines matter. Green Mountain Power's vehicle rebates apply to vehicles bought or leased through December 31, 2026, and its induction cooktop rebate covers purchases through the same date. Efficiency Vermont's weatherization offer, effective July 1, 2026, lasts only while funding lasts, so a project planned for next spring may find the money gone or the terms changed. If you are choosing between a fall install and a spring one, the fall one is the one you can price today.

Efficiency Vermont lists free appliances, products and services for income-qualified Vermonters, a free Weatherization Assistance Program through a partner, a free Virtual Home Energy Visit and $100 for DIY weatherization. We did not read the income limits for the free programs, so start with Efficiency Vermont's page. In a city where half of homes are over eighty years old, a free energy visit is a sensible first call before you collect quotes.
faq: Is Rutland in Green Mountain Power territory?
Yes, per our verified utility list. Efficiency Vermont's statewide offers apply too.
What income limit applies for the $2,000 heat pump rebate?
$89,200 for a household of four, which is Green Mountain Power's limit for counties not named in its table.
Is there a gas utility rebate in Rutland?
Only 5% of homes use piped natural gas, and Vermont Gas serves northwest Vermont, so most readers will not have one.

Efficiency Vermont's ducted heat pump discount tops out at $2,200, and Green Mountain Power's income-eligible rebate is $2,000 per condenser. For batteries, Green Mountain Power pays $850 to $950 per kW.
Does Rutland have any local rebate?
We did not find a Rutland city program. The state and Green Mountain Power offers are the ones we verified.
